column3: The burial register at Ásfjord grows every day, and medicine and graves cost whatever the sellers ask, so the poorest go without both.
This account of Ásfjord's safety comes from a first survey, so trouble the thorp keeps from newcomers may be missing from it.
Whoever walks out of Ásfjord, in any direction and at any hour, meets nothing that would justify a watch.
The thorp's plan for an army is to not be interesting to one, and everybody here can state the plan.
Ásfjord keeps no court and no gaol, and no wrong done there is written down; order is kept by whoever is armed and standing there, and when they leave, nothing keeps it.
Ásfjord cannot fund a response to anything. Any sustained pressure exhausts the thorp's capacity almost immediately and then continues.
Ásfjord is unfortified. There is no perimeter, which means the thorp cannot control entry and cannot make a chokepoint of anything.
Nobody at Ásfjord is responsible for defending the thorp; ask who is, and nobody can name anyone.
Ásfjord's defense is conventional throughout. What arrives unseen here goes undetected and therefore unanswered.
Ásfjord has not been attacked lately, and if it were, it would struggle to hold.
Nobody comes into Ásfjord and nobody leaves. The point now is to keep the sickness in, not an enemy out.
Life in the thorp goes on through the crisis: people work, eat and sleep, and the defence makes do with what is left over.
No wall marks where Ásfjord ends; the last houses simply give way to open country.
Ásfjord's books record no gang, guild or racket: what wrongdoing the thorp has, people do on their own account.
No criminal's money appears in the Elder Council's accounts at Ásfjord, so what the hall spends is spent on the thorp.
